examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Draw attribute dependencies before choosing an evaluation order. S-attributed definitions contain only synthesized attributes and suit bottom-up evaluation. L-attributed definitions permit inherited attributes from the parent and left siblings under the dependency restrictions. A reference to a right sibling can violate this order or create a cycle.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A production S→AB has B.i=A.s+2 and S.s=A.s+B.s. If A.s=3 and B.s=2B.i, find S.s.

**Answer: 13.** A.s=3 gives B.i=5, then B.s=10. Finally S.s=3+10=13. The left-to-right dependencies can be evaluated without referring to an unevaluated right sibling.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
An attribute name such as '.i' does not determine inherited versus synthesized status by itself; its defining production occurrence does.

An attribute dependency cycle prevents a straightforward valid evaluation order.
